chunks: Even so We roused them that they may question one another. One of them asked: 'How long have you stayed here?' They said: 'A day or less than a day.' 'Your Lord knows best,' they said, 'how long you have stayed. So send one of you to the town with this money of yours to look for wholesome food and bring it for you; but he should be careful not to let your presence known.'

key_terms.لِيَتَسَاءَلُوا: That they may question one another
key_terms.وَلَا يُشْعِرَنَّ: And let him not make aware

ai.seo_question: What did the Sleepers of the Cave discuss upon waking up regarding their time in the cave?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the Sleepers' transition from divine protection to active engagement with the world, sending one companion to procure sustenance while maintaining secrecy. This act of 'talaaffuf' (discretion) underscores the balance between remaining hidden from oppressive authorities and participating in daily life, a principle often linked to the concept of *Taqiyya* (prudent concealment) in Shia tradition. The dialogue emphasizes that while human perception of time is limited, God's knowledge of their true duration remains absolute, reinforcing divine sovereignty over history.
